title: Ops Orchestra: taskified admin conductor and automated support flows
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Build 'Ops Orchestra', a lightweight conductor service that composes existing admin utilities into taskified flows for support automation. The conductor will present a deterministic task graph API to the Console and Ops CLI, support safe dry-run, RBAC gating, and attach rich telemetry for cost/latency and quality regressions.

Background: We have dozens of shell scripts, ad-hoc admin endpoints, and brittle runbooks. On-call and first-line support frequently need to chain multiple utilities in the right order (e.g., revoke tokens -> rotate keys -> restart agent). Current patching is manual, error-prone, and hard to observe. Previous runbook-as-tasks experiments proved the value of typed parameters and dry-run but lacked a unified execution conductor and global safety policies.

Goals:
- Provide a task graph execution service that can orchestrate existing admin utilities as idempotent steps with typed inputs/outputs.
- Add safety gates (RBAC, approval step, rate limits, canary scope) and a required dry-run path when the actor is not an SRE.
- Emit structured telemetry: step-level latency, success/failure codes, cost-estimates (approx tokens/DB ops), and per-request provenance.
- Surface the conductor in Console as an 'Ops Flow' run panel and expose via Ops CLI for automation.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting utilities into a new language. We will wrap existing endpoints/CLI commands as task adapters.
- Replacing full incident orchestration tooling (Pager integration) in this phase.

Design (high-level):
- Task adapters: small shim services that declare typed inputs/outputs and a semantic idempotency token. Adapters will be lightweight and point to existing admin endpoints or invoke small operator binaries.
- Flow manifest: YAML/JSON describing a DAG of tasks, retry policies, human approval nodes, and safety attributes (blast radius tag, data sensitivity).
- Conductor API: RunFlow/start/dryrun/status/step-logs/cancel. Conductor executes tasks via adapters with a pluggable sandbox (container vs process) and enforces RBAC.
- Safety engine: policy layer for rate-limits, allowed-scopes-per-role, and automatic rollback hints for common failure classes.
- Telemetry: each step emits structured events to observed service (trace_id, flow_id, step_id, before/after snapshot references).

Trade-offs and rationale:
- We prefer adapter wrappers vs rewriting so adoption is incremental. This keeps rollout risk low.
- We will implement a minimal sandbox (process-level containerization + network restrictions) initially; full container isolation is planned for later.
- Strongly-typed manifests allow static checks at commit-time (Console linting and preflight).

Acceptance criteria:
- Implement conductor API with start/dryrun/status and step-logs endpoints.
- Implement 6 example adapters (revoke-token, rotate-key, restart-agent, clear-kv-prefix, refresh-config, collect-diagnostics).
- UX in Console: run/dryrun toggle, step-by-step logs, and approval modal for flows with 'high' blast radius.
- Telemetry: step latency histogram + error rate dashboard and at least one alert on spike-in-failure-rate.
- Security review completed and on by default for flows that touch production-scoped keys.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal dogfood: enable only for SREs in staging.
2) Add RBAC and auto-dryrun for non-SREs.
3) Gradual opt-in for support agents with audit logging.
4) Public beta for teams via Console toggle.

Notes/implementation tasks:
- Add manifest linter into admin-ci to block unsafe flow merges.
- Provide CLI 'opsctl flow run --dry-run' and 'opsctl flow explain' subcommands.
- Add automatic fallback steps (e.g., if rotate-key fails, run detect-rotational-inconsistency).
